name: business-resources
intro: The business resources a primary asset holds, and for each attack outcome the loss drivers OpenCRQ recommends when the outcome hits a resource: 35 pairings of an outcome with a resource. A pairing absent here is one the model holds to be unrealistic. OpenCRQ derives a range from the financial profile only for the drivers the pairings of a scenario recommend: its outcome with the resources of the scenario, those its primary assets hold when they are chosen for it. Any other driver of the catalog can still be priced, with a range entered by hand.

cells: The processes and services your organisation runs for itself: production, logistics, internal support, back office.
Services and products other organisations or customers rely on under contract, SLA or delivery commitment: SaaS, managed services, contracted deliveries, platforms clients run their business on.
Equipment, plants, buildings, OT and ICS, vehicles: anything an attack can physically destroy or render untrustworthy.
Any data identifying people: customers, employees, patients, users, including special categories such as health or biometrics and non-card financial identifiers.
Cardholder and payment data an attacker can use to carry out fraud: PANs, track and chip data, card verification values, payment credentials. Tick it alone, it covers the personal data it contains.
Your own competitive information: trade secrets, R&D, source code, formulas, pricing, M&A plans, negotiation positions, models and their weights.
Other organisations' confidential data you hold under contract or NDA: B2B customer data, professional-services files, partner designs, government-client data, licensed corpora.
Your organisation's money and the authority to move it: bank balances, treasury, payment runs, payroll, the mandates and approvals that release funds, crypto assets.
Money and assets you hold or move for clients: client accounts, escrow, portfolios under management, securities in custody, payment float.

A function or a data set a regulator with fining power supervises: essential or important entities under NIS2, DORA, CER, telecom, energy or health regulators, export-controlled or defence technical data. Tick it together with the resource it regulates.
